A.explanation: Gives only $\text{s}^{-2}$ and omits the $\text{m}^2$ left after dividing pressure by density.

B.explanation: Keeps $\text{kg}$ incorrectly; the $\text{kg}$ in pressure and in density cancel in the division.

C.explanation: Keeps $\text{kg}^2$ and adds an extra $\text{m}^2$ in the numerator, which does not follow from $\text{kg m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2}$ divided by $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.

D.explanation: Matches $\text{m}^2\text{s}^{-2}$ obtained when $\text{kg}$ cancels and $\text{m}^{-1}$ divided by $\text{m}^{-3}$ leaves $\text{m}^2$.

hints: Notice the quantity is $\frac{\text{pressure}}{\text{density}}$, so you need the SI base units of each part before dividing.
Recall pressure as $\frac{\text{force}}{\text{area}}$ with force in $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ and area in $\text{m}^2$, giving $\text{kg m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2}$.
Recall density as $\frac{\text{mass}}{\text{volume}}$ in $\text{kg m}^{-3}$, then divide and cancel $\text{kg}$ to see what powers of $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$ remain.
walkthrough: Write each quantity in base units: pressure $= \frac{\text{force}}{\text{area}}$.
Force has units $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ and area has units $\text{m}^2$, so pressure has units $\frac{\text{kg m s}^{-2}}{\text{m}^2} = \text{kg m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2}$.
Divide the two unit expressions: $\frac{\text{kg m}^{-1}\text{s}^{-2}}{\text{kg m}^{-3}}$.
Cancel $\text{kg}$ top and bottom and combine powers of $\text{m}$: $\text{m}^{-1-(-3)}\text{s}^{-2} = \text{m}^2\text{s}^{-2}$.
The unit $\text{m}^2\text{s}^{-2}$ uses only SI base units $\text{m}$, $\text{s}$ with correct powers. This is option D.
